html:
On 26 January 1788 the First Fleet, eleven British ships carrying convicts, marines and officials, raised the British flag at Sydney Cove. It began the European colonisation of Australia.

Britain could no longer ship convicts to America after the American War of Independence, and its prisons were overflowing. James Cook had reported on the coast at Botany Bay in 1770. The fleet left Portsmouth in May 1787 under Captain Arthur Phillip, with over 1,400 people, about half of them convicts. Botany Bay proved poor, so Phillip moved a few kilometres north to a deep harbour, Port Jackson, and its cove, Sydney Cove.

The land belonged to the Eora and neighbouring peoples. The early colony nearly starved before more ships came. Contact was devastating for Aboriginal people: the smallpox epidemic of 1789 killed many, and land was taken by force. The fleet began eighty years of convict transportation. 26 January is now Australia Day, which many Aboriginal Australians mark instead as Invasion Day; see Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: On 26 January 1788 the First Fleet, eleven British ships carrying convicts, marines and officials, raised the British flag at Sydney Cove. It began the European colonisation of Australia.
